question: Explain how gas chromatography separates the components of a mixture.
answer: The mixture is vaporised and carried by an inert gas (mobile phase) through a column containing a liquid or solid stationary phase; components interact with the stationary phase to different extents, so they have different retention times
mark_scheme: MP1 1 mark: Mobile phase is an inert gas and stationary phase is in the column. Accept: inert gas; carrier gas; helium; nitrogen; argon; mobile phase. MP2 1 mark: Different retention times from different interactions. Accept: retention time; retention times; different retention times; different times; take different times; emerge at different times. Allow any wording that conveys the idea, including common alternatives, correct hedged answers ('I think ...') and clearly intended spelling. Ignore extra correct detail. No mark if the idea is negated, contradicted, or the response gives two different answers.
model_answer: The vaporised mixture is carried through a long coiled column by an inert carrier gas such as helium; compounds that are more soluble in the stationary phase or have a stronger attraction to it are retained longer, so each component emerges after a different retention time and is detected.
common_misconceptions: Students say that the mobile phase is a liquid in gas chromatography.

question: Explain how the retention time and a mass spectrometer can be used together (GC–MS) to identify the compounds in a mixture.
